title: Alice's Adventures in Wonderland
description: A bored girl follows a White Rabbit underground, changes size until she no longer knows who she is, and wakes when she finally tells the court of Wonderland what it is: a pack of cards.

cover.alt: Alice shields herself as the pack of cards flies at her
cover.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: Down the rabbit-hole
elements.text: Bored on a riverbank, Alice sees a White Rabbit check a watch and runs after it, straight down a hole that turns into a long slow fall past cupboards and shelves.

metadata.source_quote: Oh dear! Oh dear! I shall be late!

image.alt: The White Rabbit calls Alice 'Mary Ann'
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: Drink me
elements.text: In a hall of locked doors she drinks from a bottle and shrinks, eats a cake and grows to nine feet. Neither size fits the little door to the garden.

metadata.source_quote: It was all very well to say “Drink me,” but the wise little Alice was not going to do that in a hurry.

image.alt: Alice, curious and a little lost
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: The pool of tears
elements.text: Giant Alice cries, shrinks again and finds herself swimming in her own tears with a Mouse, a Duck, a Dodo and a crowd of other creatures.

image.alt: Alice swimming in the pool of tears among birds and animals
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: The Caucus-race
elements.text: To get dry, the Dodo organises a race with no start, no finish and no rules, and declares that everyone has won.

metadata.source_quote: “Everybody has won, and all must have prizes.”

image.alt: The Caucus-race: the Dodo and the dripping animals run in a circle around Alice
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: Advice from a Caterpillar
elements.text: A Caterpillar on a mushroom asks Alice who she is and is unimpressed when she cannot say. He tells her one side of the mushroom makes you grow and the other shrink.

image.alt: The Caterpillar on his mushroom, Alice peering up at him
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: Pig and pepper
elements.text: In the Duchess's kitchen the air is full of pepper and flying saucepans. Alice rescues the howling baby, which turns into a pig in her arms and trots away.

image.alt: The Duchess's kitchen, full of pepper and flying saucepans
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: The Cheshire Cat's directions
elements.text: A grinning Cat in a tree tells Alice that it doesn't matter which way she goes if she doesn't know where she wants to get to, and that everyone here is mad.

metadata.source_quote: “Would you tell me, please, which way I ought to go from here?”

image.alt: The Cheshire Cat in its tree, Alice asking which way to go
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: A mad tea-party
elements.text: The Hatter, the March Hare and a sleeping Dormouse sit at an endless tea-table, stuck at six o'clock since the Hatter quarrelled with Time.

metadata.source_quote: “Take some more tea,” the March Hare said to Alice, very earnestly.

image.alt: The Mad Tea-Party
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: The Queen's croquet-ground
elements.text: Gardeners paint white roses red; the Queen of Hearts sentences everyone to death; croquet is played with flamingos for mallets and hedgehogs for balls.

image.alt: Gardeners painting the white roses red as the Queen arrives
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: The Gryphon and the Mock Turtle
elements.text: The Gryphon takes Alice to the weeping Mock Turtle, who tells of his school under the sea and teaches her the Lobster Quadrille.

image.alt: Alice by the sea with the Gryphon and the Mock Turtle
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: Who stole the tarts?
elements.text: At the Knave of Hearts' trial the evidence is nonsense, the jury writes everything down on slates, and Alice starts growing again in the witness box.

metadata.source_quote: “Begin at the beginning,” the King said gravely, “and go on till you come to the end: then stop.”

image.alt: The trial of the Knave of Hearts
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: A pack of cards
elements.text: When the Queen calls for Alice's head, Alice, now full size, calls the court a pack of cards. They fly at her, and she wakes on the riverbank with leaves on her face.

metadata.source_quote: “Who cares for you?” said Alice, (she had grown to her full size by this time.) “You’re nothing but a pack of cards!”

image.alt: Alice shields herself as the pack of cards flies at her
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: Alice
elements.text: A polite, curious, well-read girl who argues with everyone she meets. She keeps losing her size and her lessons, never her nerve for long.

metadata.source_quote: I almost wish I hadn’t gone down that rabbit-hole—and yet—and yet—it’s rather curious, you know, this sort of life!

image.alt: Alice, curious and a little lost
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: The White Rabbit
elements.text: A nervous rabbit in a waistcoat, always late, who serves the Queen as herald and mistakes Alice for his housemaid, Mary Ann.

metadata.source_quote: Oh my ears and whiskers, how late it’s getting!

image.alt: The White Rabbit calls Alice 'Mary Ann'
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: The Caterpillar
elements.text: A languid, contrary caterpillar smoking a hookah on a mushroom, who answers questions with questions.

image.alt: The Caterpillar on his mushroom, Alice peering up at him
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: The Cheshire Cat
elements.text: The Duchess's cat, which grins, vanishes at will and is the only creature in Wonderland that explains the place honestly.

metadata.source_quote: “Well! I’ve often seen a cat without a grin,” thought Alice; “but a grin without a cat!

image.alt: The Cheshire Cat vanishing until only its grin remains
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: The Hatter
elements.text: Host of the mad tea-party, condemned to six o'clock for ever, fond of riddles without answers.

image.alt: The Mad Tea-Party
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: The Queen of Hearts
elements.text: A furious card queen who settles every difficulty by ordering an execution. Nobody is actually executed.

image.alt: The King and Queen of Hearts at the croquet ground
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: The Gryphon and the Mock Turtle
elements.text: An offhand Gryphon and a sobbing Mock Turtle who remember school under the sea: Reeling, Writhing and Uglification.

image.alt: Alice by the sea with the Gryphon and the Mock Turtle
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: The rabbit-hole and the hall of doors
elements.text: A deep well-like hole and a long low hall of locked doors, with a tiny door to the loveliest garden Alice ever saw.

image.alt: The White Rabbit calls Alice 'Mary Ann'
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: The Duchess's kitchen
elements.text: A kitchen full of smoke and pepper, a sneezing Duchess, a grinning cat and a cook throwing everything within reach.

image.alt: The Duchess's kitchen, full of pepper and flying saucepans
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: The March Hare's house
elements.text: A house with ear-shaped chimneys and a fur-thatched roof, and a long table laid for tea under a tree.

image.alt: The Mad Tea-Party
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: The Queen's garden and croquet-ground
elements.text: The garden Alice wanted to reach all along: rose trees painted red, card soldiers, and a croquet-ground all ridges and furrows.

image.alt: Gardeners painting the white roses red as the Queen arrives
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: The court of justice
elements.text: A courtroom with the King as judge, twelve creatures as jury and a dish of tarts on the table as evidence.

image.alt: The trial of the Knave of Hearts
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: Size as instability
elements.text: Food and drink in Wonderland change your size, and the right size is never available when you need it. Alice learns to manage the mushroom.

image.alt: The baby turns into a pig in Alice's arms
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: Nonsense logic
elements.text: Every argument in Wonderland follows rules, just not the right ones: words are taken literally, premises are false, and questions are answered with other questions.

image.alt: The Cheshire Cat in its tree, Alice asking which way to go
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: The court of cards
elements.text: Power in Wonderland belongs to playing cards: a King, a Queen, a Knave, soldiers and gardeners shaped like flat cards. It lasts only while someone takes it seriously.

image.alt: The King and Queen of Hearts at the croquet ground
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: Who in the world am I?
elements.text: Identity is the question the book keeps returning to: Alice tests herself with multiplication tables and poems, and gets them wrong.

metadata.source_quote: Who in the world am I? Ah, that’s the great puzzle!

image.alt: Alice, curious and a little lost
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: Rules without law
elements.text: Every creature is sure of the rules, and the rules change when it suits them. Authority in Wonderland is loud, arbitrary and empty.

image.alt: Gardeners painting the white roses red as the Queen arrives
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: Every moral, or none
elements.text: The Duchess finds a moral in everything; the book refuses to have one, and makes fun of the improving verses Victorian children learned by heart.

metadata.source_quote: Everything’s got a moral, if only you can find it.

image.alt: The Duchess's kitchen, full of pepper and flying saucepans
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: Growing up as talking back
elements.text: Alice wakes by refusing to be frightened, and the dream collapses. Growing up is the courage to call nonsense by its name.

image.alt: Alice shields herself as the pack of cards flies at her
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: Victorian lesson-verse
elements.text: Alice's mangled recitations ("How doth the little crocodile") parody poems every Victorian child memorised, such as Isaac Watts's "How doth the little busy bee".

elements.title: Alice Liddell
elements.text: The story began as a tale told to the three Liddell sisters on a boat trip from Oxford on 4 July 1862; Alice Liddell asked Dodgson to write it down.

elements.title: Mad as a hatter
elements.text: The Hatter and the March Hare take their madness from two English sayings: "mad as a hatter" and "mad as a March hare".

image.alt: The Mad Tea-Party
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.
